title: The colony eats its bed to bare stems, then starves on it
question: Same bed, same seed, frame 150,000 -- A has the shipped ant colony in it, B is the identical bed with the ants simply removed. Bug Z6 says every bed starves its colony; the open question was whether it OVERGRAZES or CANNOT REACH the food. Does A read to you as a bed that has been eaten, or as a bed that failed to grow?
context_md: COUNTS (the numbers under the pictures). Default box, seed 3, RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1, 150,000 frames of a 300,000-frame run. A (with the colony): 469 animals born, 518 died, EVERY death starvation; colony peaked at 137 ants around frame 108,000; 5 plants, 445 plant cells, seed bank 0 -- and it is still 445 cells with zero ants alive at frame 300,000, so it never recovers. B (ants removed, nothing else changed): 99 plants, 10,883 plant cells, 211 seeds in the ground. Priced in food the ant's own gut would digest, at 300,000 frames: 90 edible cells fed against 1,934 unfed, i.e. 4%. The other half of the finding is that the founders starve FIRST, at frame 3,600-4,500, with 44,640 J standing in the bed against their whole 10,400 J endowment -- so the colony dies twice, of opposite things. Full write-up: Reports/colony-starvation-separated-2026-09-08.md

items.label: with the colony: 5 plants, 445 cells, 3 ants left
